A1.justification: Both PDFs describe NewtonBench and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Matching retained content across renumbering and appendix additions supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 11 LLMs, including symbolic accuracy, RMSLE, noise sensitivity, and code-assistance experiments in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark evaluations and adds empirical results for symbolic-regression baselines, evaluator diagnostics, and physical-plausibility analyses.

M1.justification: The documented expression-tree mutation procedure, Equation/Model formalization, agent workflows, code tool, and primary Nemotron judge remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 and Appendix C prompts match. Revised benchmark equations and additional analyses do not introduce a new discovery algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions retain 324 tasks across 12 domains, but v1 Table 4 and v2 Table 5 contain substantial replacements of shifted laws in thermal conduction, radioactive decay, elasticity, and calorimetry. For example, Hooke-law variants containing additive constants and sine terms become multi-term power laws. This materially revises the tested task content despite unchanged domain names and task counts.

E2.justification: v2 Appendix E.5 adds evaluated PySR and LLM-SR comparators. PySR is compared with LLMs across all 12 domains in the vanilla-equation setting; LLM-SR with GPT-4.1-mini is evaluated only on sound-speed tasks (Figure 21 and Table 21). The original 11-LLM comparator roster remains.

E3.justification: Appendix A.4.2 changes radioactive-decay N0 sampling from [10^-4, 10^-2] to [1, 100], heat-transfer temperature-difference sampling from [10^-2, 10^2] to [10, 1000], and removes Hooke-law k sampling. New protocols include varying judge demonstrations, a DataBlind hint control, and 2,500-iteration LLM-SR evaluation with relaxed symbolic-accuracy postprocessing. Main agent temperature and interaction limits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds system-complexity counts, performance stratification by physical plausibility, and judge style-robustness, error, and few-shot analyses (Appendices A.2, A.3.4, and A.5). Appendix E.1 expands the existing DataBlind finding with explicit model-specific results, a with/without-hint comparison, and a failure example. The original noise, code-budget, and four agent case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix A.1 retains four independent runs, standard deviations in the main results table, and 95% confidence intervals in plots. No changed run-count, seed, or uncertainty-estimation practice is documented. Revised means and uncertainty values are result changes.

E6.justification: Table 2, four domain heatmaps, and several aggregate analyses change extensively. For example, vanilla GPT-5 overall symbolic accuracy changes from 72.9% to 75.9%, and hard/complex-system accuracy from 29.9% to 40.3%. These accompany revised tasks and sampling, so they are not demonstrated same-setting gains. New results include baseline comparisons, plausibility-stratified performance, and judge accuracy across demonstration counts.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3.4 adds a definition of new singularities and explicit domain, regularity, positivity, and structural criteria for three physical-plausibility levels. The core Equation/Model definitions, expression-tree evaluation reasoning, and Appendix E.2 solvability assumptions A0–A4 and proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: a scalable, memorization-resistant interactive benchmark, fragile frontier-model discovery, and the code-assistance paradox. Terminology and reported scores change without redefining these main claims.

C2.justification: v1's brief physical-plausibility caveat is expanded into detailed admissibility levels and suggested uses. New Appendix E.6 distinguishes discovery within predefined apparatus from designing experiments and discusses limits relative to modern data-intensive science. The Ethics Statement adds an untested generalization argument for chemistry and biology, while Appendix E.5 interprets symbolic regression's numerical-fidelity versus symbolic-recovery tradeoff.

D1.justification: v2 documents assisting-equation and operation counts, a DataBlind prompt example, and LLM-SR's backbone, iteration budget, estimated API usage, and output postprocessing. Primary prompts, API platforms, agent settings, and code/data access information remain unchanged. These additions improve documentation without establishing new resource availability.

R1.justification: Section 3.1 removes the MARS and possible-world philosophical grounding while adopting counterfactual-physics terminology. Related work adds PhysGym and SR-Scientist, and the plausibility discussion adds mechanics and thermodynamics references. Table 1 and the broader benchmark positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The revision replaces 'metaphysical shifts' with 'counterfactual law shifts,' rewrites the short curation-motivation passage, and adds appendix subsections. The main section sequence and most original prose, prompts, case studies, and proofs are retained.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual presentation with plausibility heatmaps (Figure 7), an active/passive exploration diagram (Figure 20), a six-panel PySR comparison (Figure 21), and new tables for complexity, plausibility, judge diagnostics, DataBlind tests, and LLM-SR. Existing displays largely retain their structure, with some axis and ordering changes; numerical replacements alone are covered under E6.

improvement.justification: Additional evaluator diagnostics, symbolic-regression comparisons, and explicit physical and experimental limitations make v2 easier to assess. These benefits are tempered by restricted baseline comparability: LLM-SR is tested only on sound-speed tasks with relaxed symbolic-accuracy criteria. Results are also incompletely synchronized: v2 Table 19 retains Fourier's 29.29% accuracy while Figure 3 reports 42.8%. The net improvement in validation and transparency is therefore limited.
